THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ADITYA KUMAR  MOHAPATRA  ORDER 11.11.2024 Order No.

This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual /Physical Mode).
2.
Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner and learned Counsel for the State.
Perused the records.

3. This is an application under Section 438, Cr.P.C. filed by the Petitioner for anticipatory bail,
involving offence punishable under Sections 468/420 of I.P.C. in G.R. Case No.2035 of 2023 of the Court of learned S.D.J.M., Kendrapara arising out of Mahakalapada P.S. Case No.203 of 2023.
4.
It is stated by learned counsel for the Petitioner that the informant and the present Petitioner are related to each other.
He further contended that as per the F.I.R. allegation, the Petitioner has withdrawn money which the late father of the petitioner as well as the informant is entitled to.

Learned counsel for the Petitioner further submitted that although the money has been transferred to the account of the present Petitioner, however, the same is lying in the bank account of the Petitioner.
He further contended that no intention of cheating anybody.

5. Considering the submissions made by learned counsel appearing for the Petitioner, on a careful examination of the materials on record, although I am not inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the Petitioner, however it is observed that, in the event the Petitioner surrenders and moves for bail before the learned court in seisin over the matter within a period of three weeks from today, he shall be released on bail on such terms and conditions as the learned Magistrate may deem just and Nityananda Mohapatra vs State Of Odisha .....

While imposing conditions the learned court below shall also impose the conditions that the aforesaid amount of Rs.3,00,000/- shall be deposited before the trial court which shall be given in a fixed deposit of a nationalized bank and as such the deposit shall be subject to the final outcome of the trial.
Violation of any of the terms and conditions shall entail cancellation of the bail.
6. The ABLAPL is disposed of accordingly.
7. Urgent certified copy of this order be granted as per rules.
